title: What Is OpenAI Decisions API? A Practical Guide
gist: A Hugging Face community guide describes OpenAI's Decisions API, introduced at DevDay 2026 in limited preview, as a specialized GPT-6 Luna endpoint that picks from developer-defined answers in roughly 150 ms (about 10x faster than regular GPT-6 Luna, per secondhand coverage) for classification, routing and agent next-step choices. The piece relies on third-party reporting, repeatedly promotes a similarly named, unaffiliated 'Decisions API' product, and a reader comment questions the linked domain, so its claims should be treated as unofficial.

insights.claim: OpenAI introduced a Decisions API at DevDay 2026 that, per public coverage, runs on a specialized version of GPT-6 Luna, accepts text or image context, and returns a selection from a developer-defined set of answers.
insights.speaker: bna
insights.so_what: OpenAI is productizing high-frequency, low-token control calls, opening a new API revenue line priced per decision rather than per generated text.
insights.quote: Public coverage describes it as a specialized version of GPT-6 Luna that is designed for fast, single decisions.
insights.locator: OpenAI introduced the API at DevDay 2026

insights.claim: The author argues the Decisions API turns a pattern developers already hand-build with prompts, JSON schemas and post-processing into a first-class API concept.
insights.speaker: bna
insights.so_what: Platform providers absorbing common middleware patterns threatens startups selling prompt-routing and classification tooling.
insights.quote: it turns a pattern that developers have been building with prompts, JSON schemas, and post-processing into a first-class API concept
insights.locator: The launch matters because it turns

insights.claim: A decision API differs from JSON mode because the answer space is bounded before inference and the endpoint is optimized for selecting among those answers, rather than formatting free generation as JSON afterward.
insights.speaker: bna
insights.so_what: Purpose-built selection models can be smaller and cheaper than generative models, shifting inference mix toward lightweight calls.
insights.quote: the answer space is bounded before inference, and the endpoint is optimized around selecting among those answers

insights.claim: The author frames the launch as part of a broader industry shift from asking models to write something toward asking models to make one small, typed judgment.
insights.speaker: bna
insights.so_what: If agent loops are dominated by many cheap decision calls, API volume growth may outpace token-revenue growth.
insights.quote: part of a shift from “ask a model to write something” toward “ask a model to make one small, typed judgment.”

insights.claim: DevDay coverage reports roughly 150 milliseconds latency for the Decisions API, about ten times faster than querying GPT-6 Luna through the regular API, though the author warns these are marketing numbers.
insights.speaker: bna
insights.so_what: Sub-200ms decisions make model calls viable inside real-time agent loops, expanding the number of model invocations per task.
insights.quote: reports roughly 150 milliseconds for Decisions API and describes it as about ten times faster than asking GPT-6 Luna through the regular API

insights.claim: A decision layer can cut costs by classifying request difficulty or risk and routing easy work away from expensive frontier models, but input context, repeated calls, retries and observability still cost money.
insights.speaker: bna
insights.so_what: Model-routing layers compress average revenue per request for frontier models while increasing total call volume.
insights.quote: Not every request needs a frontier model.

insights.claim: OpenAI's preview pricing for the Decisions API was not fully public at the time of writing, so unit-economics forecasts built on it are placeholders.
insights.speaker: bna
insights.so_what: Pricing disclosure is the key watch item for assessing the product's revenue impact.
insights.locator: OpenAI's preview pricing was not fully public

insights.claim: The author proposes a five-layer agent architecture: orchestrator, generative model, decision model, policy and permissions, and action and audit, with the decision model never substituting for the policy layer.
insights.speaker: bna
insights.so_what: Separate policy and audit layers point to durable demand for agent governance, permissions and observability tooling.
insights.quote: It can say that an action appears safe; it cannot grant permission that your policy engine did not grant.
insights.locator: Where it belongs in an agent architecture

insights.claim: A stronger model can plan an agent's goal while a fast decision model chooses among approved next steps, making agents easier to inspect.
insights.speaker: bna
insights.so_what: Planner-plus-selector designs favor vendors offering a tiered model lineup over single-model providers.

insights.claim: The author's safety rule is that model judgment intersected with deterministic policy defines the executable path: models judge meaning while code owns authority.
insights.speaker: bna
insights.so_what: Enterprises will keep deterministic authorization outside LLMs, limiting how far model vendors can expand into security and compliance.
insights.quote: model judgment ∩ deterministic policy = executable path

insights.claim: Confidence scores returned by decision models should not be treated as calibrated probabilities; teams should measure accuracy, false-positive and false-negative rates, and calibration by class, language and segment, and start in shadow mode for decisions affecting money, access or safety.
insights.speaker: bna
insights.so_what: Evaluation and shadow-deployment needs slow enterprise automation rollouts and support demand for eval tooling.
insights.quote: Confidence is a routing signal, not proof.

insights.claim: The article compares OpenAI's limited-preview product with a separately branded 'Decisions API' that already offers a public playground, typed Choice/Score outputs with probabilities, and public pricing plans.
insights.speaker: bna
insights.so_what: Smaller vendors are crowding the decision-model niche and may face naming and distribution pressure from OpenAI's entry.
insights.locator: OpenAI Decisions API versus Decisions API

insights.claim: The guide is built on secondhand sources such as The Decoder and Pasquale Pillitteri's analysis rather than official documentation, and the author admits linking a placeholder site after a reader asked whether the domain belonged to another company.
insights.speaker: bna
insights.so_what: SEO-driven community posts can conflate unrelated products with OpenAI launches; verify against official sources before acting.
insights.quote: I’ve temporarily linked to a site I found as a reference
